english_u1l1.q: If the Present Continuous form is correct, put a tick. If it's wrong, correct the spelling or change it to the Present Simple: (1) I'm siting (2) John is swimming (5) We're liking Egypt (8) I'm knowning (12) I'm understanding.
english_u1l1.answer: (1) I'm sitting  (2) John is swimming ✓  (5) We like Egypt  (8) I know  (12) I understand.
solution: (1) خطأ إملائيّ فقط: sit تُضاعِف التاء → I'm sitting.
(2) صحيح؛ swim فعلٌ حركيّ يجوز في المستمرّ → tick.
(5) like فعلٌ ساكن (stative) لا يأتي في المستمرّ → We like Egypt.
(8) know فعلٌ ساكن (مع خطأ إملائيّ) → I know.
(12) understand فعلٌ ساكن → I understand.

english_u1l1.q: Complete with the Present Perfect Simple or the Present Perfect Continuous: 1) Rachel, why are your hands so soft? Because I ___ . 3) George, you look tired. Yes, I ___ . 5) Are the floors clean? Yes, Jane ___ them. 6) Why are your eyes red, Mike? Because I ___ .
english_u1l1.answer: 1) have been doing the washing-up  3) have been cutting the grass  5) has swept  6) have been peeling the onions.
solution: الأسئلة التي تفسّر حالةً حاضرة (يدان ناعمتان، تَعَب، عينان حمراوان) تأخذ التامّ المستمرّ للتركيز على النشاط: have been + V-ing.
السؤال عن نتيجةٍ مكتملة (هل النظافة تمّت؟) يأخذ التامّ البسيط: Jane has swept them.

english_u1l1.q: Complete with the Present Perfect Simple or Past Simple: A: I saw Jack last night. B: Oh really. I (1) ___ (not/see) him for months. — A: (2) ___ (you/ever/win) a competition? B: Yes, I (3) ___ (win) a writing competition in 2006. — A: Is that a new tab? B: Yes, I (4) ___ (just/buy) it.
english_u1l1.answer: (1) haven't seen  (2) Have you ever won  (3) won  (4) have just bought.
solution: (1) و(2) و(4): زمنٌ غير محدَّد أو أثرٌ مستمرّ → مضارع تامّ.
(3) زمنٌ ماضٍ محدَّد (in 2006) → ماضٍ بسيط: won.

english_u1l1.q: Which verb form do we use for: 1) a completed action in the past  2) things which started in the past and are true now  3) recent actions when we don't say exactly when  4) recent actions when we say exactly when?
english_u1l1.answer: 1) Past Simple  2) Present Perfect  3) Present Perfect  4) Past Simple.

english_u1l1.q: Choose the correct homophone: 'No one knows ___ the ___ will be fine tomorrow.'
solution: whether = سواء/إن (أداة)، weather = الطقس؛ فالجملة: No one knows whether the weather will be fine tomorrow.

english_u1l1.q: Choose the correct word between brackets: 1) Which (way/weigh) should we use to (way/weigh) the goods? 4) The man is enjoying his time with his (son/sun) on the beach under the (son/sun). 6) The teacher asked the students to (right/write) down the (right/write) answer.
english_u1l1.answer: 1) way / weigh   4) son / sun   6) write / right.
solution: way (طريقة) ثمّ weigh (يزِن)؛ son (ابن) ثمّ sun (شمس)؛ write (يكتب) ثمّ right (الصحيح).

english_u1l1.q: Complete with the correct form of the word in brackets: 1) Individuals have ___ dreams. (vary)  2) Everyone endeavours to make dreams a ___. (real)  3) Future plans and ___s have a great importance. (decide)  4) Gaining your boss's confidence is a great ___. (accomplish)  5) I went to a counselor for ___ on my career. (guide)

Match each phrasal verb with its meaning: reach out / fit in / get into / follow through / run into / keep up with — (a) be accepted by other people in a group (b) encounter problems unexpectedly (c) start something and finish it satisfactorily (d) start to become interested in something (e) stay updated about something (f) offer help and support to someone.
english_u1l1.answer: reach out = f, fit in = a, get into = d, follow through = c, run into = b, keep up with = e.

english_u1l1.q: In the reading, the word 'aptitude' means:
solution: aptitude = الاستعداد الفطريّ / القدرة أو المهارة الطبيعيّة، وهو مرآةٌ لشخصيّة الطفل ونقاط قوّته وضعفه.

english_u1l1.q: What factors should be taken into consideration to decide a future career?
english_u1l1.answer: The child's aptitude (personality, strengths and weaknesses, revealed by an aptitude test), the child's genuine interest in the field, the availability of courses leading to the desired career, avoiding peer pressure, and suitable remuneration that matches the child's aspirations and provides a comfortable life.
solution: النصّ يعدّد: الاستعداد الفطريّ (aptitude) الذي يكشفه اختبارٌ مصمَّم، والاهتمام الحقيقيّ بالمجال، وتوافر الدورات المؤدّية للمهنة، والحذر من ضغط الأقران، والأجر (remuneration) الملائم — وإن لم يكن الأهمّ.

english_u1l1.q: What do researchers recommend for choosing our future career? And how can demotivation affect the child?
english_u1l1.answer: Researchers recommend self-reflection and guided activities, through which we can find our core values and a clearer path towards the right career. Demotivation (rejecting all of the child's ideas) might have a negative impact on the child's mental health.

english_u1l1.q: Complete with words from the article: 1) Parents play a vital ___ in the career development of their children. 2) Parents should study very well the ___ of their children. 3) There should be leading ___ to help children choose the best job. 4) Most people encourage their children based on the ___ that profession brings.
According to the text, a job's remuneration is the single most important factor when choosing a career.
solution: النصّ يقول صراحةً: 'Although it should not be the most important, remuneration of a career holds value' — فالأجر مهمٌّ لكنّه ليس الأهمّ.

english_u1l1.q: A child can easily get swayed by peer pressure into choosing the career that the majority is opting for.
solution: قال علماء النفس في النصّ إنّه من السهل جدّاً أن يتأثّر الطفل بضغط الأقران فيختار مهنة الأغلبيّة بدلاً من الأنسب له.

english_u1l1.q: Your friend is a heavy smoker. Give him advice to quit smoking, using an advice expression and a suitable response.
english_u1l1.answer: — If I were you, I would see a doctor and try to quit smoking gradually. You'd better replace the habit with sport. — Response (accepting): You're right. I'll do that. / (hesitating): Maybe you're right, but it's very hard to stop.
solution: يُستعمل قالب النصح: If I were you... / You'd better... / You should... / Try to...، ثمّ ردّ القبول (Yes, you're right, I'll do that) أو ردّ التردّد (Maybe you're right, but...).

english_u1l2.q: Preview game: choose the answer (a or b) that represents each letter of the word SUCCESS. S: self-confidence / self-doubt — U: uncertainty / understanding — C: cowardice / courage — C: clarity of purpose / confusion — E: experience / expectancy — S: sullenness / smile — S: self-acceptance / self-rejection.
english_u1l2.answer: S = self-confidence, U = understanding, C = courage, C = clarity of purpose, E = experience, S = smile, S = self-acceptance.

english_u1l2.q: Put the phrases A–H in the correct gap (1–8) of the text 'Stop Wishing, Start Doing'. A) a successful person must be rich  B) brings you closer at jet speed  C) in which playing to win matters  D) accomplish your goals  E) it would be preparation  F) through repetition or experience  G) to build up confidence and become successful  H) which is achievable.
solution: 1-D: means to accomplish your goals. 2-A: it is believed... that a successful person must be rich, but money cannot buy success.
3-H: a smart goal which is achievable. 4-E: if there was one secret to success, it would be preparation.
5-F: obtaining good timing is through repetition or experience. 6-G: help children to build up confidence and become successful and happy.
7-B: every step... brings you closer at jet speed. 8-C: Life is like a game in which playing to win matters more than playing not to lose.

english_u1l2.q: Match the highlighted words with their meanings: perseverance / sacrifice / trigger / inevitably / perspiration — 1) certain to happen and cannot be avoided  2) when you decide not to have something valuable to get something more important  3) to initiate or activate something  4) hard work  5) determination to keep trying in spite of difficulties.

Replace the underlined phrase with the correct form of a success idiom (back the wrong horse / ace a test / join the ranks of / on a roll / to be dead in the water): 1) His efforts didn't work; there is little hope for his project. 2) If you get a high score on your math test... 3) Our team has won ten of twelve matches; we are making a lot of progress. 4) Don't support someone you know always fails. 5) Thousands become part of the unemployed each summer.
english_u1l2.answer: 1) His project is dead in the water. 2) If you ace your math test... 3) Our team is on a roll. 4) Don't back the wrong horse. 5) ...join the ranks of the unemployed.

english_u1l2.q: Classify the -ed ending of these past verbs into /t/, /d/ or /id/: helped, believed, finished, ended, missed, wanted, educated, ordered, washed, called, needed, realized.
english_u1l2.answer: /t/: helped, finished, missed, washed.  /d/: believed, ordered, called, realized.  /id/: ended, wanted, educated, needed.
solution: /t/ بعد صوتٍ مهموس (عدا t)، /d/ بعد صوتٍ مجهور أو حركة (عدا d)، /id/ بعد /t/ أو /d/.

english_u1l2.q: In which verb is the -ed ending pronounced /id/?
solution: wanted ينتهي جذرها بصوت /t/ فتُلفظ -ed كـ /id/؛ أمّا helped وwashed فـ /t/، وbelieved فـ /d/.

english_u1l2.q: Look at these sentences and answer: 1) A woman called to report a robbery. 2) It happened when she was watching news on TV. 3) The burglar came in, picked up the handbag, emptied it out and stole her purse. 4) The family had been struggling for some time. 5) When she came into the room, the burglar had already left. — Which sentence: (a) provides a background scene? (b) is a single completed action? (c) is a series of completed actions? (d) shows the second event happened first? (e) focuses on how long an activity continued?
english_u1l2.answer: (a) background scene → 2  (b) single completed action → 1  (c) series of completed actions → 3  (d) second event happened first → 5  (e) how long an activity continued → 4.

english_u1l2.q: Complete the police interview with the Past Simple or Past Continuous: P: And what ___ (you/do) after you woke up? — P: Did anything happen while ___ (you/watch) TV? S: Yes, the phone ___ (ring). — P: What ___ (you/do) when your husband came home? S: I ___ (prepare) lunch when he came. — S: We ___ (drink) coffee. Then I ___ (put on) my raincoat and we ___ (go out). — P: Why ___ (you/put) your raincoat on? S: Because it ___ (rain).
english_u1l2.answer: did you do; were you watching; rang; were you doing; was preparing; drank; put on; went out; did you put; was raining.
solution: الماضي المستمرّ للمشهد الخلفيّ الجاري (were watching / were you doing / was preparing / was raining)، والماضي البسيط للأحداث المنجَزة (did you do, rang, drank, put on, went out, did you put).

english_u1l2.q: Fill in with a verb from (buy, discuss, develop, not take, make, feel, work) in the Past Simple, Past Perfect Simple or Past Perfect Continuous: 1) She ___ as a waitress for three years when he met her. 3) Henry did well, which was a shock because he ___ an exam before. 4) Scientists announced the new drug; they ___ it for five years. 5) By the time I got to the meeting they ___ the important issues and ___ the big decisions without me. I ___ annoyed.
english_u1l2.answer: 1) had been working  3) had not taken  4) had been developing  5) had discussed / had made / felt.
solution: 1) و4) مدّة نشاطٍ مستمرّ قبل لحظةٍ ماضية → Past Perfect Continuous.
3) و(discuss/make) في 5) حدثٌ منجَز قبل حدثٍ ماضٍ آخر → Past Perfect Simple.
(feel) في 5) ردّ فعلٍ في زمن الوصول → Past Simple: felt.

english_u1l2.q: Match the phrasal verbs with their meanings: take up / give up / carry on — a) stop, abandon  b) continue  c) start something new.
english_u1l2.answer: take up = c (start something new), give up = a (stop, abandon), carry on = b (continue).

english_u1l2.q: Make an appropriate response for each situation using congratulating / expressing-sympathy expressions: 1) Your school team has won the final. 2) You are visiting a friend who has broken his leg. 3) Your little brother got low marks. 4) Your father got a new promotion.
english_u1l2.answer: 1) Congratulations! You really deserve this honour. Very well done! Keep it up. 2) I'm sorry about what happened. You mustn't let this depress you; I'm sure you'll recover soon. 3) You mustn't let this depress you. I have no doubt that you'll do much better next time. 4) Congratulations! We are proud of you. You really deserve this honour.
solution: المواقف 1 و4 مواقف تهنئة (نجاح/ترقية)، والموقفان 2 و3 موقفا مواساة وتشجيع.

english_u1l2.q: According to the text, 'Success is 10% inspiration and 90% ___.'
solution: المقولة في النصّ: 'Success is 10% inspiration and 90% perspiration' — أي إنّ الجهد والعرق هما الأساس.

english_u1l2.q: According to the text, money can always buy you success.
solution: النصّ يقول: 'in many cases, money cannot buy you success' — فالمال وحده لا يشتري النجاح.

english_u1l2.q: The text advises us to be a 'learn it all' rather than a 'know it all'.
solution: القاعدة الذهبيّة للنجاح مواصلة التعلّم؛ فالكلمات الخطيرة الثلاث هي 'I know that'، والأصحّ أن تكون مُتعلِّماً دائماً لا مُدّعياً معرفة كلّ شيء.

english_u1l2.q: In your own words, explain what the writer means by: 'Become a learn it all rather than know it all.'
english_u1l2.answer: It means you should stay humble and keep learning all the time instead of assuming you already know everything; the moment you say 'I know that,' you stop growing, so successful people keep an open, curious mind.
